selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Where did the traveller go after leaving the gathering of the prophets?
questions.answer: He went to a place of learning with truthful and carefully thinking scholars.

questions.question: What do these scholars do for the prophets’ message?
questions.answer: They support it by giving powerful and decisive evidence.

questions.question: What did the scholars prove so clearly that doubt was pushed away?
questions.answer: They proved the truths of faith, especially that Allah exists and is One.

questions.question: What made their proofs so strong?
questions.answer: Their proofs were deep, clear, and certain, so they left no room for doubt.

questions.question: What makes their agreement even more impressive?
questions.answer: They still agreed even though they did not all have the same level of ability or the same way of looking at things.

questions.question: What happens when someone “makes night” by closing his eyes?
questions.answer: He only blocks the light from himself, not from the world.

questions.question: For how long had the scholars’ light been spreading widely?
questions.answer: It had been shining over much of the world for more than a thousand years.

questions.question: What long-term result of the scholars’ work did the traveller notice?
questions.answer: He noticed that their light had guided much of the world for more than a thousand years.

questions.question: What lesson should a student take from this passage?
questions.answer: A student should learn that true belief is supported by united, careful, and strong evidence.

questions.question: Who invited the traveller into the classroom in this passage?
questions.answer: Scholars who confirm the prophets’ message with very strong evidence invited him.

questions.question: What special qualities are given for these scholars?
questions.answer: They are deep, original, exact, pure, and very truthful.

questions.question: What words show that these scholars were serious and trustworthy?
questions.answer: They are shown as pure, truthful, careful, and highly respected.

questions.question: What does it show when many intelligent scholars agree on the basics of faith?
questions.answer: It shows that their conclusion is very reliable and hard to deny.

questions.question: What is one reason their shared conclusion carries weight?
questions.answer: Each scholar was depending on evidence that was firm and certain.

questions.question: What kind of proof did each scholar use?
questions.answer: Each one used a proof that was strong and certain.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to explain this idea?
questions.answer: It gives the picture of a person closing his own eyes and then only making things dark for himself.

questions.question: What did the traveller understand about the reach of these scholars’ light?
questions.answer: He understood that it had illuminated half the world for over a thousand years.

questions.question: For what length of time had that light continued?
questions.answer: It had continued for more than a thousand years.

questions.question: What new group does the traveller meet in this part of the journey?
questions.answer: He meets purified and truthful scholars who defend the message of the prophets.

questions.question: Who are the teachers in that classroom?
questions.answer: They are purified, very truthful scholars who confirm the prophets’ teachings.

questions.question: About how many learned people did the traveller see there?
questions.answer: He saw thousands of brilliant minds and hundreds of thousands of careful, honored scholars.

questions.question: Why is the scholars’ unity meaningful?
questions.answer: It is meaningful because so many wise people agreed on the same foundations of faith.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about rejecting all of them?
questions.answer: It implies that rejection would come from ignorance and stubborn refusal, not sound thinking.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by the example of someone shutting his eyes in daylight?
questions.answer: Refusing to see the truth does not change the truth; it only harms the person who refuses.
